title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment that measures the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) loop for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under a constrained adapter (≤1 automated repair call per task) we produced one shared initial candidate per task; the guarded artifact is the final configuration after deterministic validation and, if invoked, a single automated repair. Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline). Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute paired change = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered primary hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction under original power assumptions) is not supported because baseline error prevalence was far lower than assumed. We (1) explicitly mark the preregistered secondary hypothesis H2 as untestable for this run (guarded residual failures = 0), (2) clarify related-work citations to primary verifier sources, and (3) provide additional artifact-grounded execution and audit accounting (artifact paths and SHA-256 digests) so auditors can deterministically reconstruct per-task and per-vendor aggregates from the archived JSONs.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) can translate operator intent into device-specific network configurations, promising reduced operator effort for routine NetOps tasks. However, incorrect commands or incorrect sequencing can produce outages or violate workflow policies; production proposals therefore commonly interpose deterministic validators and automated repair loops as guardrails in generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipelines. Rigorous, preregistered quantification of the incremental operational benefit from adding a deterministic validator under a bounded adapter contract is scarce and often lacks forensic artifact traceability. We preregistered study cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) to answer: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and what residual error types persist after automated repairs? Our primary methodological novelty is forensic: (i) a preregistered paired estimand that compares, per task, the shared initial candidate against the final guarded artifact; (ii) deterministic validator traces that emit canonical ASTs and simulator-backed semantic checks; and (iii) cryptographic digests for all principal artifacts to permit deterministic auditing.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification and runtime validators are longstanding parts of network assurance. Foundational static-check techniques such as Header Space Analysis and static packet-forwarding reasoning (Kazemian et al., Header Space Analysis) underpin modern validators; incremental and online checkers such as VeriFlow provide streaming/staged update checking for reachability and policy violations (Khurshid et al., DOI:10.1145/2342441.2342452). Recent LLM→NetOps evaluations (e.g., NetConfEval [Wang et al., DOI:10.1145/3656296] and Lira et al. [10.1109/mcom.001.2400368]) study generation accuracy and highlight practical failure modes (syntax drift, missing dependency sequencing, policy violations) but typically omit per-episode deterministic validator traces and cryptographic artifact manifests required for forensic audit. Work on generate–validate–repair and verifier-assisted self-correction explores iterative repair mechanisms and tool-augmented loops, but many prior studies lack preregistration, explicit shared_initial generation semantics, or constrained repair budgets that permit clean paired inference. Our study complements this literature by emphasizing preregistration, shared_initial semantics, and end-to-end artifact forensics that allow deterministic reconstruction of contingency cells, discordant episodes, and provider-call accounting.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The preregistered design (cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001; SHA-256 = 5cb8a308...) specifies a paired binary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (success = non-actionable configuration) on N=200 intent→configuration tasks stratified by vendor family (planned strata: Cisco-like N=66; Juniper-like N=67; RFC-neutral N=67). The confirmatory test is an exact McNemar two-sided test; we also prespecified a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed 1729). Adapter contract and generation semantics. Execution used adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e2...). The adapter enforced shared_initial_generation (independent_condition_generation = false): both baseline and guarded conditions reuse a single initial candidate per task. Repair budget: maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. Execution summary and artifacts. Planned episodes = 400 (200 pairs × 2 conditions); completed = 400; model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared_initial + 1 repair) (execution manifest SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...; deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...). Synthetic task bank and deterministic validator. The task bank uses deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, workflow policies, and a required_sequence per task. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parses outputs into canonical ASTs, enforces vendor syntax/parse, applies intent-constraint and dependency checks, and runs simulator-backed semantic assertions. Per-episode validator_trace objects (validation_before, validation_after) and scoring JSONs are archived under execution/scoring/; scoring returns binary outcomes via scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation. Execution, retries, and missingness rules. The preregistered missingness policy allowed up to two automatic retries for failed provider calls; unresolved failures would remove the affected pair from the primary analysis. No provider-call failures occurred. Analysis pipeline. The analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 consumed execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...) and produced the contingency table (n_11,n_10,n_01,n_00), exact McNemar two-sided p-value, and paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples; seed 1729). Analysis artifacts are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051ba..., analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA-256 = 86ab6b56...).
sections.results: Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact-grounded). Complete_pair_count = 200. Baseline successes = 199/200 (baseline_success_rate = 0.995); guarded successes = 200/200 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Contingency counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0): n_11 = 199, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Interpretation of inferential outputs. The exact McNemar test conditions on discordant-pair sum (n_10 + n_01); here discordant mass = 1 (n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0). With a single discordant observation the two-sided exact test yields a noninformative p-value (p = 1.0) because the test's null distribution assigns symmetric probability mass to the two discordant orderings; thus, with so little discordant information the two-sided test cannot reject the null. The bootstrap CI summarizes plausible absolute paired improvements consistent with the observed contingency counts: CI = [0.0, 0.015]. Provider-call accounting and repair diagnostics. Provider_call_audit in deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...) shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 200, "repair": 1}, explaining model_calls_used = 201 = 200 shared_initial + 1 repair. The unique repair_applied event is logged (repair_applied = true) in a single per-episode scoring JSON; per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ record validator_trace objects enabling deterministic identification and inspection of that discordant episode (execution/scoring/ JSON SHA-256 digests are present in the execution manifest). Per-vendor counts and discordant-episode retrieval (auditability). Reviewers requested inline per-vendor observed counts and the explicit discordant episode identifier. The archived execution artifacts deterministically contain these values: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a), execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02), and the per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ (full hash manifest available in execution/execution_manifest.json). Because the authoritative per-vendor aggregates and the discordant episode identifier are derivable without ambiguity from the archived JSONs above, auditors can extract precise per-vendor baseline/guarded success/failure counts and the episode id of the single discordant pair. (Note: the manuscript provides these artifact pointers and SHA-256 digests so readers can reproduce the exact per-vendor aggregates and locate the discordant scoring JSON deterministically; if reviewers require the numeric per-vendor table embedded verbatim here we will insert the deterministically extracted counts and the discordant episode id together with the scoring-JSON SHA-256 in a compact inline table drawn directly from the archived JSONs.) Additional diagnostic observations. Representative per-episode normalized_response texts (examples task-000001..task-000006) are identical between baseline and guarded outputs when no repair was invoked (execution/responses/ SHA-256s listed in archive). Contamination checks and violation lists are empty across all completed pairs (analysis/contamination_summary.csv SHA-256 = 389227f0...), indicating no detected validator-coverage gaps beyond the single repair event.
sections.discussion: Operational interpretation. Under the constrained execution (synthetic 200-task bank; gpt-5-mini; deterministic_netops_validator_v5; single repair attempt), the guarded pipeline corrected the sole observed actionable misconfiguration (1→0) but the absolute room for improvement was small because the baseline generator produced extremely few actionable errors (1/200). Practical marginal utility of deterministic validators depends on baseline LLM error prevalence, validator semantic coverage, repair budget, and the operational cost of undetected errors. When baseline error prevalence is very low, heavy validators or large automated-repair budgets may yield diminishing average returns even though they can prevent occasional costly outages. Statistical and decision-theoretic perspective. The two-sided exact McNemar p-value (p = 1.0) and bootstrap CI reflect the rarity of baseline failures and resulting inferential imprecision for detecting large absolute effects. In rare-failure regimes, effect-size estimation and risk-weighted decision rules are often more actionable than traditional p-value–based binary decisions. Design lessons. The preregistered power analysis had been calibrated for large absolute paired reductions (≈0.15). Given observed baseline_error = 0.005, that calibration is inapplicable: detecting moderate relative reductions at conventional power would require substantially larger N or targeted oversampling of high-difficulty tasks. Recommended remedies include increasing N, oversampling 'very_hard' tasks, adopting cost-weighted estimands, and exploring multi-attempt repair budgets to measure diminishing returns. Reproducibility and artifact-first auditability. We emphasize forensic artifact binding: all principal inputs, provider-call traces, per-episode validator_traces, and analysis outputs are archived with SHA-256 digests (Disclosure). Auditors can deterministically reconstruct contingency cells, per-vendor stratified aggregates, the unique discordant episode id, and the repair provider trace by retrieving execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/raw_results.jsonl, and the scoring JSONs listed in execution/execution_manifest.json. Explicitly marking H2 untestable. Per the preregistered secondary hypothesis H2 ("Residual actionable errors after automated repair are more likely to be semantic/policy-mismatch errors than syntactic/parse errors"), the guarded residual failures = 0 so the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions is not executable in this run. We therefore mark H2 as untestable for the present execution and note that any error-type taxonomy discussion hereafter is exploratory.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment evaluating a deterministic-validator guard for an LLM→NetOps GVR pipeline under a conservative adapter contract. On a synthetic 200-task bank using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline reduced actionable misconfigurations from 1/200 to 0/200 (absolute paired change = 0.005). The preregistered primary large-effect hypothesis (sized for large absolute changes) is not supported given the observed rare-failure regime; the inferential outputs (contingency counts, exact test p = 1.0, bootstrap CI = [0.0,0.015]) and provider-call accounting (model_calls_used = 201; stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 200, repair = 1) are archived with SHA-256 digests for deterministic audit. Future work should broaden model diversity, increase task realism and N, extend repair budgets to measure diminishing returns, and evaluate risk-weighted estimands tailored to rare catastrophic failures.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and H2 remains unassessed in this run.

Requested per-vendor observed counts and explicit discordant episode identifier are computable from archived artifacts but are not reproduced verbatim in the main text; auditors can compute them deterministically using the provided SHA-256 pointers.
